# Results — Study 617 (Crash-Insurance-Cost)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **TAIL and
put-buying strategies bleed money every year, and that bleed is the volatility risk premium seen
from the buyer's side** — measured on the live, buyable crash-insurance product (Cambria's TAIL
ETF: ~90% intermediate US Treasuries + a laddered budget of OTM SPX puts), decomposed against its
own collateral, with the 2020 payoff episode quantified and the premium named via variance-swap
arithmetic on real ^VIX + SPY. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `c3658cfa4e95`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes: **TAIL**, **IEF**, **SPY** (auto-adjusted, **total-return** — distributions folded in) + **^VIX** (a level, not a price) |
| Window | tape 1990-01-02 → 2026-06-30 (9,191 days); TAIL era 2017-04-06 → 2026-06-30 (**9.2 years**, 2,319 daily returns, **110 complete months**) |
| Product | TAIL (Cambria Tail Risk ETF), inception 2017-04-05, expense ratio **0.59%/yr inside the NAV** — every TAIL number below is **net** of it |
| Execution / lag | TAIL buy-and-hold is a **static** position — no timing signal, hence no signal lag; the variance-premium series uses the **prior month-end VIX** against the following month's realized variance (**exactly one month of lag**, no look-ahead) |
| Costs | the SPY/TAIL blends charge **5 bps one-way × turnover** at each monthly rebalance; TAIL's ER is already inside its NAV |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** TAIL is the *surviving* dedicated tail-risk ETF —
> most of its cohort (e.g. the 2010s VIX-call and put-ladder funds) closed after bleeding out
> faster. Measuring the bleed on the survivor therefore **understates** the cost of the category:
> the bias runs *against* the claim, and the claim clears the bar anyway.

## 1 · Raw drift — what buy-and-hold crash insurance costs

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| total return since inception (net of ER) | **−49.7%** |
| CAGR | **−7.17%/yr** (ann vol 14.8%) |
| daily mean | −2.53 bps/day · HAC *t* = −1.49 (NW lags 8) |
| **monthly mean** | **−56.52 bps/month** · **HAC *t* = −2.17** (n = 110) |

A dollar of crash insurance bought at launch in April 2017 is **50 cents** today — and that is
the *net-of-fee, total-return, distributions-reinvested* number. The monthly drift clears the
desk's bar on its own (|*t*| = 2.17 ≥ 2), with the sign pointing at the **seller**.

## 2 · Decomposition — the put sleeve's drag, isolated from bond duration

TAIL ≈ a Treasury sleeve + an OTM SPX put ladder, so `tail = α + β·IEF` isolates what the *puts*
cost from what *bonds* did (2022's bond bear is β's problem, not the insurance bill).

| frequency | α (drag) | HAC *t*(α) | β(IEF) | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| daily | −3.08 bps/d = **−7.75%/yr** | −1.98 | 1.05 (*t* +12.9, R² 0.226) | 2,319 |
| **monthly (headline)** | −64.09 bps/mo = **−7.69%/yr** | **−3.28** | 0.73 | 110 |
| pre-COVID sub-period (→ 2020-02-19) | **−14.70%/yr** | −2.50 | — | 721 |
| post-COVID sub-period (2020-07-01 →) | −8.07%/yr | −1.75 | — | 1,506 |

The insurance bill is **≈ −7.7%/yr** against TAIL's own collateral, significant at monthly
frequency (**HAC *t* = −3.28**) and negative in *both* sub-periods — the crash itself excluded
from each, so neither leg owes its sign to the jackpot. (Of the −7.7, 0.59 pp is the fee; the
rest is the put ladder.)

## 3 · The 2020 payoff — the one time the insurance paid

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| TAIL, SPY peak (2020-02-19) → TAIL's own high (2020-04-02) | **+28.47%** |
| SPY over the crash (2020-02-19 → 2020-03-23) | **−33.72%** |
| jackpot fully given back (first close below the pre-crash level) | **2021-03-05** — **337 days** after the peak |
| at-inception (2017) holder at the COVID peak | **+4.22%** |
| the same holder at the end of tape | **−49.67%** |

The insurance *worked* — +28% while the market fell a third. But the bleed had already eaten the
first three years: at the very top of the best crash payoff in the fund's life, an at-inception
holder was up just **+4.22%** overall. Within **337 days** the entire jackpot was gone.

## 4 · The premium named — buyer-side variance premium from real ^VIX + SPY

Variance-swap arithmetic on real tapes (a **model-derived** series, labeled as such — not an
option backtest): each month the buyer pays implied variance `IV = (VIX_{m−1 end}/100)²/12`
(known before the month starts) and receives realized variance `RV = Σ daily squared SPY log
returns of month m`.

| window | mean RV−IV (ann var pts) | HAC *t* | vol-points | HAC *t* | buyer wins |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1993-02 → 2026-06 (401 months)** | **−0.95** | **−3.12** | **−3.79** | **−9.42** | **16.2%** of months |
| TAIL era (2017-05 → 2026-06, 110 months) | −0.67 | −1.06 | −3.62 | −4.44 | 17.3% |

Average implied vol **20.98%** vs realized **18.58%**: the buyer of volatility pays ~2.4 vol
points a year more than variance delivers, loses in **5 months out of 6**, and the gap is
significant over 33 years (*t* = −3.12 in variance units, −9.42 in vol points). This **is** the
volatility risk premium of studies [92-easy-money](../92-easy-money/) and
[63-free-fall](../63-free-fall/) — read from the paying side. TAIL's −7.7%/yr alpha is that
premium (plus fees) flowing through a live NAV.

## 5 · Third axis — has ANY buy-and-hold TAIL cohort ever come out ahead?

Every month-end entry cohort (110 of them), held to 2026-06-30, total-return:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| cohorts ahead today | **1 of 110 (0.9%)** — best **+0.10%**, entered 2025-01-31 |
| median cohort | **−34.1%** · worst **−49.4%** |
| cohorts EVER ahead at any month-end along the way | 71.8% (almost all via the COVID spike) |

**Net of the 2020 win, nobody came out ahead.** 72% of cohorts *were* ahead at some point — the
COVID spike lifted every pre-2020 entry — but every one of them gave it back. The single cohort
above water today is a 2025 entry up +0.10%; no cohort that actually caught the crash kept the
win.

## 6 · Tradability — the insurance inside a portfolio

Monthly-rebalanced SPY/TAIL blends vs 100% SPY over TAIL's life, **5 bps one-way × turnover**
charged at each rebalance (TAIL's ER inside its NAV); net-of-cost CAGRs.

| blend | CAGR | vs 100% SPY | CAGR drag | max DD | COVID DD |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 95/5 SPY/TAIL | +14.06%/yr | +15.12%/yr | **−1.06 pp/yr** | −22.9% vs −23.9% | −17.6% vs −19.4% |
| 90/10 SPY/TAIL | +12.99%/yr | +15.12%/yr | **−2.13 pp/yr** | −21.9% vs −23.9% | −15.8% vs −19.4% |
| 80/20 SPY/TAIL | +10.84%/yr | +15.12%/yr | **−4.28 pp/yr** | −19.9% vs −23.9% | −12.1% vs −19.4% |

The hedge does what it says in the crash month (COVID drawdown trimmed by 1.8–7.3 pp) — and
charges 1–4+ pp of CAGR *every* year for it. Over the full window every blend ends behind, and
the max-drawdown improvement is 1–4 pp against a CAGR bill of the same size, paid annually.

## 7 · Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic synthetic world (bond sleeve + put sleeve with a **planted** net insurance bleed;
`bleed = 0` = actuarially fair insurance), **20 seeds per setting** — never cited for a stamp:

| planted bleed | mean recovered α | mean HAC *t* | flagged at \|t\| ≥ 2 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **0%/yr (fair insurance)** | −0.21%/yr | **−0.31** | 5% of seeds (nominal) |
| **−5%/yr (planted)** | **−5.21%/yr** | **−5.81** | **100%** of seeds |

Fair insurance does not get flagged (5% false positives — exactly the nominal size); a planted
5%/yr bleed is recovered in magnitude and lit up in every seed. The real-tape −7.7%/yr at
*t* = −3.28 is therefore a measurement, not a construction artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The bleed clears the bar on the real tape three separate ways: TAIL's
  monthly drift (**HAC *t* = −2.17**), its monthly alpha against its own collateral
  (**−7.69%/yr, HAC *t* = −3.28**, negative in both crash-free sub-periods), and the buyer-side
  variance premium on 33 years of real ^VIX+SPY (**HAC *t* = −3.12** in variance units, −9.42 in
  vol points, buyer loses 5 months in 6). The premium is real — and the *sign* says it belongs
  to the seller (studies [92](../92-easy-money/) and [63](../63-free-fall/), both Real).
  Survivorship runs *against* the claim here (TAIL is the surviving tail fund) and it clears
  anyway.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE** (for the buyer). Buy-and-hold crash insurance costs ≈7.7%/yr against
  its own collateral, net of fee; every SPY/TAIL blend drags CAGR by 1–4+ pp/yr at 5 bps costs;
  the one jackpot in the fund's life was fully given back in 337 days. There is no deployable
  edge on the long side — the harvestable side of this premium is the *seller's*, already graded
  (Real / Fragile) in 92 and 63.
- **"Did the 2020 jackpot leave anyone ahead?" — BUSTED.** 1 of 110 month-end cohorts is above
  water today (+0.10%, a 2025 entry that never saw the crash); 72% of cohorts were ahead
  mid-flight — almost all via the COVID spike — and every one gave it back. The at-inception
  buyer was up just +4.22% at the very top of the payoff.
